endorsements.quote: Specifically, clinical departments should implement algorithmic impact assessments before adopting new cardiovascular AI tools, ensuring that the local patient demographics match the tool's training data.

Furthermore, health systems must establish multidisciplinary AI ethics committees composed of cardiologists, data scientists, and community patient advocates to provide human-in-the-loop surveillance of AI outputs.

unlisted_practices: Establish a federally coordinated, interoperable national cardiovascular AI data repository linking de-identified data from health systems and public health agencies.
Mandate standardized demographic performance bias audits of AI tools before and after deployment.
Require independent ethics review, human-in-the-loop oversight, and public reporting for AI in cardiovascular care.
Provide federally supported AI literacy and ethics training for clinicians and public health professionals.
Establish regional AI equity committees including community representatives.
Require the FDA to mandate standardized demographic performance reporting for AI-enabled devices.
Develop standardized fairness metrics applicable across diverse clinical settings.
Use privacy-preserving and federated learning approaches for international collaboration to improve algorithm performance across diverse populations.

screen.reason: Editorial proposing a policy-oriented governance framework (the AI-CVD Equity Act) for ethical and equitable AI governance in cardiovascular disease management.
